newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda T-bill discount rate rises as demand falls.
newsitem.headline: Uganda T-bill discount rate rises as demand falls.

text.p: The discount rate on Uganda's main group of treasury bills rose last week after demand for them declined, the central Bank of Uganda said on Tuesday.
Bank of Uganda said the discount rate on the 91-day bills rose to 12.19 percent from 11.5 percent.
"Demand for the bills eased a bit, hence the rise," an official at the central bank told Reuters.
The bank said the average weighted price for the bills fell slightly to 96.96 percent from 97.13, previously.
BOU auctions the 91-day bills daily to mostly commercial banks, insurance firms and the national social security fund.
The bank said 4.0 billion shillings ($3.64 million) were put up for sale at the auction, and all of it was bought. The same amount would be auctioned this week, it added.
It also auctions 182-, 273- and 364-day bills once a month.
